brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
An oven-dried green tea from Jingxian county in Anhui, regarded as the best and most concentrated production of the province's jian teas.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Its grades run from Tikui through special-grade jian to ordinary jian in grades one to six, twelve levels in all, and Tikui is often counted with the special grade. The Tikui grade was rated a quality tea in 1985 and a Chinese famous tea in 1986. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Finished by oven drying rather than pan firing (hongqing).
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Vivid green, even and glossy, with visible down.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: A lasting, tender and high aroma with a fresh, mellow taste.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
